goal: Let Codex download a file from a URL and keep the user informed with live progress during that plugin-managed download.
requirements: Provide a Codex-compatible plugin package stored on E:.
Start a download without blocking progress queries.
Return downloaded bytes, total bytes, percentage when known, speed, ETA when available, status, and destination.
Resume only after validating the same URL fingerprint, strong ETag, and correct Content-Range.
The skill defaults to an absolute downloads folder in the real user workspace; the tool never guesses the workspace from its own cwd.
Do not overwrite existing destination files.
Keep runtime dependencies limited to Python standard library.
Support cancellation, optional expected SHA-256, bounded concurrency, and no overwrite at final publication.
Assess practical product value, distribution, and small-scale monetization honestly.
Build a novice-friendly standalone visual workbench with batch deduplication, queueing and category folders.
Provide privacy-safe receipts/posters and a clearly labelled local demo for short-video demonstrations.
Prepare a low-price delivery/service experiment without inventing sales or payment capability.
features: MCP tools: start_download, get_download_progress, cancel_download, list_downloads.
Waited polling and concise conversation updates without unchanged-status spam.
Strong ETag resume, cross-process destination locks, and no-overwrite publication.
Optional SHA-256 validation, terminal failure states, frozen terminal speed, and redacted URL queries.
Four active transfers and 100 session-local history entries.
Standalone authenticated local workbench; Windows x64 one-file executable.
Up to 50 links per batch, deduplication, category folders, safe skip and cancellation.
Private CSV receipts, filename-free share posters and explicitly labelled own-file demos.
Nine MCP tools; quickstart, scenario templates and social marketing drafts.
known_limitations: The plugin can track only transfers started through its own MCP tool, not downloads performed by other tools, package managers, or the operating system.
Progress percentage and ETA require a known content length; otherwise only downloaded bytes and speed are available.
Public plugin directory publication may require a hosted HTTPS MCP server and review; this build targets local Codex use first.
Task IDs and history do not survive a server restart; retained partial files can be recovered by resubmitting the URL and destination.
Cancellation is cooperative; a blocked network read can delay confirmation.
POSIX final publication requires hard links and has not been run on a real macOS/Linux host.
No automatic retries or persistent queue; multi-GB endurance and real customer willingness to pay remain unverified.
status: 0.3.0 implemented and verified; installed locally with nine MCP tools. User confirmed low-price delivery pack plus optional setup assistance; no checkout or social store configured.

validation.frozen_windows_executable: Startup, bundled assets, three actual demo downloads, valid ZIP, CSV and clean shutdown verified on Windows 11 x64
validation.ui_validation: Desktop browser demo and poster rendering checked; mobile breakpoint implemented but not tested on a real phone
validation.legacy_reproduction: 0.1.0 reported completed for a 110000-byte file whose content differed from the server file

product_assessment: Worth sharing as a focused free community utility; standalone paid demand is unproven. Consider optional setup or workflow customization services after real-user validation.
success_criteria: Plugin package loads through the installed Codex CLI.
Real MCP stdio calls complete a download and support listing and cancellation.
Regression tests verify changed content, truncation, concurrency, final-file races, checksums and cancellation.
Local marketplace can load the updated plugin and the fix branch is pushed for review.
